title: Rights of intended third-party beneficiaries
summary: A third-party beneficiary is someone who may claim a benefit under a contract made by other people. The key question is whether the agreement and governing law give that person an enforceable right rather than merely an incidental advantage.
notes:
Lawrence concerns a promise to pay another person’s debt. Seaver concerns a promise to provide for someone in a will. Those cases explore why the person benefited may sue despite not making the bargain. The two Sisney cases involve distinct arrangements and different evidence about an intention to create enforceable rights. A contract serving the public or benefiting an identifiable group does not automatically give every member a private contract action.

Identify the promisor, promisee, proposed beneficiary, precise performance promised, and evidence of intended enforceability. The beneficiary’s interest must be tied to that contract. Questions about vesting and later modification arise only after identifying a right capable of vesting.

topics.third-party-beneficiaries: The agreement can create enforceable rights for a person outside the original exchange.
